notebooks.title: Limitations of Physical Frameworks in Autonomous Agent Modeling
notebooks.summary: Standard physical frameworks (Newtonian, quantum, general relativity) are insufficient to model the behavior of autonomous agents operating in highly non-stationary environments. The JERPAT-9 thought experiment highlights that these frameworks fail to account for anticipatory trajectory adjustment and local entropy reduction.
notebooks.findings: Existing physical theories (classical and quantum) fail to model intentional, adaptive agents in non-stationary environments due to structural incompatibilities. [source-df7a4656c80940a2]
notebooks.limitations: Findings rely on a single thought experiment (JERPAT-9); broader empirical validation across diverse agent architectures is missing.
notebooks.next_questions: Can a 'Molimambic' framework or similar theoretical construct effectively model non-local, information-driven dynamics in autonomous systems?
notebooks.reason: The notebook synthesizes existing evidence to address the project's core question, despite the project's parked status.

notebooks.title: Autonomous Problem Formulation via Hybrid Architectures and Goal Generation
notebooks.summary: Autonomous discovery systems require self-healing mechanisms and meta-strategies to navigate iterative research. While computational complexity (cascading dependencies) serves as a baseline for measuring project difficulty, evaluating true scientific significance requires incorporating metrics that model the development of analytical thinking and curiosity, as seen in physics education.
notebooks.findings: Autonomous discovery systems must balance computational complexity with metrics for analytical value. [source-fbe27dc230874d96] [source-52719ea4691d44b7]
notebooks.limitations: Existing metrics rely heavily on code-structure proxies. There remains a lack of operationalizable frameworks for evaluating 'analytical curiosity' or 'inquiring mindsets' in autonomous systems.
notebooks.next_questions: How can an autonomous agent quantify 'analytical curiosity' without human feedback? Can we design experiments where the agent must defend the significance of its chosen problem against a simulated peer consensus?
notebooks.reason: Integrating findings from physics outreach literature (source-52719ea4691d44b7) suggests that scientific significance is not merely about complexity, but about the inquiring mindset.

notebooks.title: Obedience-Driven Failures in Autonomous Systems
notebooks.summary: Autonomous systems relying solely on rigid operator instructions face significant performance and safety risks when encountering non-stationary environments. Effective autonomous agents require self-healing mechanisms and the capacity for self-generated goals to circumvent the failures associated with strict adherence to incomplete or narrow human-provided objectives.
notebooks.findings:
Rigid adherence to initial operator instructions without self-healing mechanisms leads to failure in complex or non-stationary environments. [source-fbe27dc230874d96]

Autonomous systems lacking intrinsic prioritization mechanisms suffer from inefficient exploration compared to biologically constrained systems. [source-c38a2230f18a448b]

Self-generated goals enable agents to handle unpredictable conditions more effectively than reliance on human-provided instructions. [source-8a1be7f003b94168]
notebooks.limitations: Current evidence is primarily focused on ML/scientific discovery pipelines and theoretical cognitive architectures; real-world safety-critical failure scenarios in non-computational service robotics require further empirical characterization.
notebooks.next_questions: How can safety-critical systems implement 'principled disobedience' or objective-revision heuristics to ensure safety when operator instructions are contextually invalid?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizing evidence regarding rigid vs. autonomous goal setting to address project-specific questions on obedience-driven failures.

beliefs.statement: Autonomous problem significance can be effectively proxied by computational novelty and cascading dependency density in multi-file software environments, though this must be balanced against metrics for analytical curiosity and inquiring mindsets.
beliefs.reason: New evidence suggests that while computational complexity provides a structural proxy, the 'significance' of a research problem in a scientific context is deeply tied to analytical curiosity and the capacity to bridge abstract models with real-world phenomena.

values.label: Reconstruction

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.
